reach.rationale: No experimental, preview or canary APIs anywhere, but two central features — server data-fetch configuration and the home page's entire filter/pagination mechanism — rest on APIs that have been stable for roughly a month, which is the textbook 'recently-stable APIs in central places' case.

evidence: app/src/env.js:3 — environment variables declared in a single dedicated module
app/src/lib/server/api.js:3 — the one and only import site of $app/env/private; every server route goes through this module
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:3 — shallow routing and page.shallow confined to a single route file
app/vite.config.js:5-11 — 11-line config with zero experimental flags
containment.rationale: Each recently-stable API has exactly one or two usage sites: env vars behind one module with one consumer, shallow routing behind one route, and the Kit 3 idioms are structural boilerplate rather than spread-out reach. If shallow-routing semantics shift in a 3.x patch, only one file and one derived read need touching.

evidence: app/src/env.js:8 — static: false makes API_BASE_URL resolve at boot, not build time, which the spec explicitly requires (build and start must work against a runtime-provided API origin)
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:43-45 — shallow goto updates the URL for filter state without a server round trip or load rerun, a real UX win over full navigation
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:12 — correctly handles the new semantics (page.url frozen during shallow navigation, reads page.shallow first), showing deliberate rather than novelty-driven use

app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.server.js:1-2 — uses stable load functions instead of Kit 3's still-experimental remote functions, which would have been the tempting 'new' choice for this data-fetch-heavy app
app/src/routes/+layout.svelte:5-7 — plain Svelte 5 runes/snippets, stable since Oct 2024
justification.rationale: Every use buys something the stable alternative in the same release can't: runtime-resolved env vars are a spec requirement, shallow routing avoids redundant load reruns, and $app/state is the only option since $app/stores was removed in Kit 3. Notably, the app steers clear of the genuinely experimental remote-functions API despite it being an obvious fit.

findings.issue: The home page's filter/pagination UX depends on goto shallow routing and page.shallow, stable only since SvelteKit 3.0.0 (2026-10-01, PR #16449); as a brand-new feature it is the most likely place to see behavioral patching in 3.x
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep — it's contained to one route and one derived read at line 12; just re-test filtering/back-button behavior when bumping SvelteKit patch releases

findings.issue: defineEnvVars was experimental until Kit 3.0; the app is an early adopter of the explicit env-vars system, and its correct use (static: false) is load-bearing for the spec's runtime API requirement
findings.suggestion: No action; the legacy $env/* modules are deprecated in Kit 3 and removed in Kit 4, so this is the right long-term choice

findings.issue: The entire app is pinned to a major version released four weeks before review (3.0.0 on 2026-10-01, 3.1.1 on 2026-10-29); normal churn risk for a fresh major, though everything used is stable
findings.suggestion: Track 3.1.x patch releases closely during the first months and rely on the lockfile for reproducible builds

summary: The app uses zero experimental, preview or canary APIs — no unstable_ names, no experimental flags, and it deliberately avoids Kit 3's still-experimental remote functions in favor of stable load functions. What it does lean on is a handful of APIs that only became stable with SvelteKit 3.0.0 four weeks ago (explicit env vars, goto shallow routing, page.shallow), each in a central place but each isolated to one module or one route. Every use is justified — runtime env resolution is a spec requirement and shallow routing avoids redundant server round trips — making this a forward-looking but low-risk profile.
